transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, I don't want to sound difficult or anything. 

I'm here because... well, for the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing, or maybe holding back, parts of my dad’s lab results. I know how that sounds, I really do. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I just... I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I work as a phlebotomist, so I'm used to looking at these things, and it’s just really wearing me down. 

Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay.

When you look at your dad's lab results, do you actually see the numbers changing in front of your eyes, or is it more that you believe they've been altered even though the numbers appear the same to you?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I don't see the numbers moving or... or morphing on the screen or anything like that. I promise I'm not seeing things. I know how that would sound, and I really don't want you to think I'm... well, you know, seeing things that aren't there. 

It's just that when I look at the final report, the numbers on the page are already wrong. Like someone went into the computer system and altered them before I even opened the file. The numbers themselves sit perfectly still on the screen, but I just know they aren't the real results. 

Is that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making it sound worse than it is.

When people like your doctors or family tell you that the lab results haven't been changed and the numbers are correct, do you think there's any possibility they could be right, or are you completely certain that the results have been altered?

I... I really wish I could just agree with them. I know it would make things so much easier for everyone, and I really hate being a bother to my family and the clinic staff. 

But... well, like I mentioned earlier, I've spent this whole past year trying to prove this. And no matter how many times my family or the other doctors sit me down and tell me the numbers are fine, I just... I can't just let it go, because I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. I am completely certain that someone is changing or holding back parts of his results. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds incredibly stubborn of me, and I really don't want to be a difficult patient. It's just... carrying this around and trying to get people to see what's happening, it's really wearing me down. 

Is it okay that I'm being this honest with you? I hope I'm not coming across the wrong way. I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly.
Beyond the concerns about your dad's lab results being changed, do you have other worries that people are acting against you or trying to harm you in other ways?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I... I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I think people are out to get me, or trying to hurt me. I promise I don't think anything like that at all. 

Everyone at the clinic, and just people in general, they're all perfectly nice to me. It's really just... strictly this one specific thing with my dad's chart. I don't feel unsafe or targeted in my own life, I swear. I just want to make sure his numbers are right, you know? 

I hope that makes sense. Did I answer that okay? I just really don't want you to think I'm... well, thinking everyone in the world is against me, because I'm definitely not.

When you think about how the lab results are being changed, do you have a clear understanding of who specifically is doing this and exactly how they're doing it, or is it more unclear to you how the process works?

I... well, I don't really know exactly who is doing it. I mean, I work in a clinic myself, so I know how the systems work, and I know how many people have access to the electronic records. It could be anyone in the IT department, or a records coordinator, or... I don't know. 

I really try not to point fingers or accuse specific people, because I don't want to get anyone in trouble if I'm wrong about who it is. I just know that someone, somewhere in the system, is altering the numbers before they get finalized in his chart. As for how, they just... they just type in different numbers, I guess. 

I'm sorry I don't have a better answer for you. I know that's probably not very helpful. Does that make sense, though? I just don't want to sound like I'm coming up with wild theories about specific people when I don't have all the facts about who exactly is sitting at the keyboard.

If we were to do a completely independent lab test on your dad's results, done at a different hospital or lab facility with no connection to your current clinic, and those results matched what the clinic is showing now, would that change your mind about whether the numbers are being altered?

I... oh, wow. Um. I know you're trying to help, and I really, really appreciate you suggesting that. I know it sounds like such a logical solution, and I'd love to just say yes, that would fix everything. I really want to be agreeable here.

But... honestly? I've been trying to prove this for a whole year now. And it's just... it's really wearing me down. I feel like I've been running in circles, and even if we went somewhere else, I just... I know what I saw originally. The chart doesn't match. And I feel terrible saying this, I really do, because I know how frustrating it must be for everyone, including you, to hear me say this. 

But I just don't think a new test would change my mind, because it wouldn't change the fact that someone in the system altered or held back parts of those specific results from before. 

I'm so sorry. I know that's not the answer you were hoping for, and I really don't want to be difficult or dismiss your ideas. It's a really good idea, truly. I just... I can't let go of what I know happened. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope you're not upset with me for saying no to your suggestion.

You mentioned you've been trying to prove this for a year now. During that time, have there been any moments where you've wondered if maybe you could be mistaken about the lab results being altered, or has it always felt absolutely certain to you?

I... oh, I really wish I could say yes. I know it would sound so much more reasonable if I told you that I’ve second-guessed myself. And believe me, I've tried to. When literally every doctor and all my family members keep telling me that his numbers are perfectly fine and that I must be mistaken, I really, really want to agree with them. I hate upsetting my family, and I definitely don't want to be a nuisance to the doctors. 

But... for this whole past year, I’ve been trying so hard to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his results. And no matter how many times people tell me everything is fine, I just... I know what I saw. The chart doesn’t match what I saw originally. It's just always felt absolutely certain to me, and carrying this around is really wearing me down. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the right answer, and I worry it makes me sound incredibly stubborn. I really don't mean to be. Does that make sense why I feel so stuck? I just hope you don't think badly of me for not being able to let it go.

When you think about your dad's lab results being altered, is there any part of you that wonders if there could be an innocent explanation - like maybe a technical glitch, or maybe you misremembered what you saw the first time - or does it always feel completely impossible that you could be wrong about this?

I... I know how it sounds, and I really, really wish I could say it was just a computer glitch or that I just remembered it wrong. I know that would be the easiest explanation for everyone, and it would make things so much simpler for the clinic and for my family. I hate being the person causing all this fuss. 

But... I've been doing this for a year now, trying to prove that someone is changing or holding back those parts of his results. And I just... I know what I saw. The chart doesn't match. I really wish it did, because then I wouldn't have to keep fighting this, and it wouldn't be wearing me down so much. But I just can't bring myself to say it was an innocent mistake when I know in my heart it wasn't. 

I'm so sorry if that makes me sound unreasonable. I really don't want to be difficult. Do you... do you understand why I can't just chalk it up to a glitch, even though I really want to? I just hope you don't think I'm crazy for being so sure about this.

When you think about this situation with your dad's lab results, do you ever wonder if maybe your mind could be playing tricks on you, or creating a pattern that isn't really there - even though it feels completely real to you right now?

I... oh, goodness. I know why you're asking that, and honestly, it's a very fair question. I know people's minds can do strange things, especially when they're stressed, and I'd be the first to admit I've been incredibly stressed out lately. I really want to be the kind of patient who says, "Yes, maybe it's all in my head," because I know that's what everyone wants to hear. 

But... I've been a phlebotomist for years. I know how to read these things. And for this entire past year, I've just been trying so, so hard to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his lab results. And I promise you, I'm not trying to make things up or see patterns that aren't there. It's just that no matter how many doctors or family members sit me down and tell me the numbers are fine, I just... I know what I saw originally. The chart they have now just doesn't match what I saw. 

I'm so sorry. I know I keep saying the same thing, and I really don't want to frustrate you. It's just wearing me down so much, carrying this around for a year. Do you... do you think less of me for not being able to just accept that my mind might be playing tricks on me? I really hope you don't think I'm just being difficult on purpose.

Besides the concern about your dad's lab results being altered, are there any other situations in your life - at work, with friends, online, or anywhere else - where you feel like something suspicious or wrong is happening that other people don't seem to notice or believe?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. I really hope it doesn't come across like I'm just suspicious of everything, because I promise I'm not like that at all. 

Everything at work is perfectly fine, and my friends are wonderful. I don't think anyone is doing anything wrong anywhere else, not online or in my personal life. It's truly just... just this one specific situation with my dad's clinic. 

I'm actually a very trusting person normally, I swear. I really don't go around looking for conspiracies or trying to cause trouble for people in my everyday life. I just go to work, do my job, and try to be a good person. I hope that's a good sign? Like, the fact that it's just this one isolated thing? I really want you to know I'm otherwise completely level-headed... I hope you can believe that about me. Does that make sense?

Over this past year while you've been concerned about your dad's lab results, have you noticed any changes in how you think about yourself - like feeling like you have special abilities or insights that other people don't have, or feeling like certain things are happening specifically to you or about you in ways that others don't understand?

Oh, um... no. No, nothing like that at all. I don't think I have any kind of special powers or anything. I'm just a regular person. I mean, I know my job, I know how to read labs because I do it every day, but that's just training, you know? It's not a superpower or anything. 

And I definitely don't think things are happening specifically to me, like... like I'm the center of some big plot. I know it's just about my dad's chart. I'm just a daughter trying to figure out what happened with her dad's medical records. 

I really hope I haven't said anything that made you think I felt... I don't know, grand or important or something? I'm just a normal, everyday person who happens to be stuck in this really frustrating situation. I try really hard to stay grounded. I hope you can see that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of who I am.

If you were to sit down right now and really think hard about it, is there even the tiniest possibility - like 1% - that you could be wrong about the lab results being altered, or does it feel absolutely impossible that you could be mistaken?

I... oh, I really, really wish I could give you that one percent. I know that's what a reasonable person would say, and I want so badly to be a good patient and just say yes, maybe I'm wrong. I don't want to be difficult or stubborn. 

But... if I'm being completely honest with you, and I really want to be honest... I just can't find that one percent. I'm so sorry. I know it probably sounds terrible, and I hate feeling like I'm disappointing you. 

It's just... like I was saying earlier, for this entire past year, I've been trying so hard to prove that someone in that clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his results. And I listen to the doctors, I really do, and I hear my family when they tell me the numbers are fine. But I just know that the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. It feels absolutely impossible that I could be mistaken about it. 

I really wish I was wrong, honestly, because it's just wearing me down so much. It's so exhausting carrying this around. Does that make me sound completely awful? I really hope you aren't upset with me for not being able to concede that one percent... I just have to be truthful about what I know I saw. Is it okay that I'm being this honest with you?
